title: Pizza Margherita
subtitle: The classic Neapolitan tomato and mozzarella pizza
excerpt: Pizza Margherita is a Neapolitan pizza topped with tomato passata, fresh mozzarella, and basil. The toppings are simple, so the quality of each one matters. Use good passata, fresh mozzarella (not the block kind), and add the basil after baking.
sourceNotes: Pizza Margherita is one of the most documented pizzas in Italian culinary history, named after Queen Margherita of Savoy and associated with Neapolitan pizzaiolo Raffaele Esposito (1889). The recipe is codified by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana and listed in the EU Traditional Specialities Guaranteed register.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the dough 24 hours ahead (see 24-hour pizza dough). Tear the mozzarella and drain on kitchen paper 30 minutes before topping.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan or conventional, maximum oven setting. Preheat for at least 45 minutes with a pizza stone or heavy baking tray inside.

glossaryTerms.definition: The raised rim or crust edge of a Neapolitan pizza, which puffs and chars during baking.

content.text: Pizza Margherita is tomato, mozzarella, and basil on a thin disc of dough with a puffed, lightly charred

at the edge. It is the version most Italians would call pizza, and it rewards good ingredients more than any technique. The toppings go on cold dough, the pizza bakes in a very hot oven for 8 to 10 minutes, and the basil goes on after it comes out.
The recipe assumes you have dough ready. Use the 24-hour pizza dough recipe and pull the balls out of the fridge 2 hours before you plan to bake.

items.prepNote: each about 210 g, at room temperature
fresh, drained and torn into chunks

content.text: Place a pizza stone or heavy baking tray on the highest shelf of your oven and heat to the maximum setting (at least 250°C). Preheat for 45 minutes.
Season the passata with salt and stir. You will use about 3 tablespoons per pizza.
Stretch one dough ball on a lightly floured surface to a rough 30 cm disc. Leave a 2 cm border at the edge.
Spread the passata over the disc in a thin, even layer using the back of a spoon. Scatter the mozzarella over the top and drizzle with a little olive oil.
Slide the pizza onto the hot stone or tray. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is charred at the edges and the mozzarella is bubbling and browning in spots.
Remove from the oven. Scatter fresh basil leaves over the top and drizzle with a little more olive oil. Eat immediately.

Pizza Margherita is the benchmark against which every other pizza is measured. The story that it was named for Queen Margherita of Savoy in 1889 is well documented, though similar pizzas existed before that date in Naples. What defines the version today is restraint: three toppings, a thin crust, and very high heat.
